Forged|1.warmup: Why we warm up: cold muscles and stiff joints lift less and get hurt more. Spend 8 to 10 minutes on this. Do the warm-up movements in order, using only your bodyweight or a very light load, and move through the full range slowly. Then do 2 to 3 ramp-up sets of your first main lift: about 50 percent of your working weight for 5 reps, 70 percent for 3 reps, 85 percent for 1 to 2 reps. The warm-up should leave you feeling warmer, looser and a little more awake, not tired.
Forged|1.finisher: Cool-down: do not skip this, it helps your body shift out of work mode. Walk slowly for 3 minutes until your breathing returns to normal. Then spend 2 minutes stretching the muscles you just trained. Hold each stretch about 30 seconds, breathe slowly, and stop at mild tension, never pain.
Forged|1.notes: Purpose: heavy, simple, full-body strength work. This is the core of the plan. Day A leads with the squat or leg press pattern. New to the gym? Here is how to read your workout. A set is a group of reps with a rest after it. RPE is how hard a set feels on a 1 to 10 scale, and RIR means reps in reserve, how many more good reps you could still do. Stopping with 1 to 2 reps in reserve (RPE 8 to 9) is the sweet spot: hard enough to grow, safe enough to keep good form. Choose a weight you could lift 1 to 2 more times with solid form. If you are unsure, start lighter, because it is easy to add weight next time. Form beats weight every time. If your form breaks, stop the set and rest. Rest 2 to 3 minutes between main sets so your muscles are ready to go again. Use the time to sip water and breathe. To progress, once you hit the top of the listed rep range on every set with good form, add the smallest weight increase available (about 2 to 5 pounds) next session. Every fourth week is a deload week: use lighter weights and fewer sets so your body can absorb the work. This is planned, so it does not mean you are slacking. Too hard? Cut the sets by one, lower the weight, or swap to the easier alternate. Too easy? Slow down the lowering phase to 3 seconds before adding weight. What to expect: mild muscle soreness 1 to 2 days later is normal, especially in your first few weeks. Sharp, pinching or joint pain is not. If something hurts in a way that feels wrong, stop that movement and use the alternate in the app. This is general coaching, not medical advice, so check with a doctor first if you have an injury or a health condition.

Forged|2.finisher: Finish with 5 minutes of slow breathing. Lie on your back or sit comfortably, breathe in for 4 seconds, out for 6 seconds. This slows your heart rate and helps you recover.
Forged|2.notes: Purpose: recovery day. Easy movement sends blood to tired muscles and helps you feel better for the next session. Everything is done at home with no equipment. Easy effort only. Finish feeling better than you started. If you feel good, resist the urge to turn it into a workout. That is how people stall.

Warrior|5.warmup: Why we warm up: your heart, lungs and joints need a few minutes to get ready for harder work. Spend 8 to 10 minutes. Do the warm-up movements in order at an easy pace, then do one or two practice rounds at about half effort so your body knows what is coming. You should be breathing a little harder and feel warm by the end, but not worn out.
Warrior|5.finisher: Cool-down: walk slowly for 3 minutes until your breathing and heart rate settle. Breathe in through your nose and out slowly through your mouth. Drink water. Feeling a bit tired is normal. Feeling dizzy or sick is not, so sit down and rest.
Warrior|5.notes: Purpose: boxing-style conditioning to build stamina and coordination. Move through the circuit in order and rest only as listed. Keep your hands up, shoulders relaxed and feet moving. Quality beats speed: sloppy rounds just wear you out. Expect to be breathing hard. What to expect: mild muscle soreness 1 to 2 days later is normal, especially in your first few weeks. Sharp, pinching or joint pain is not. If something hurts in a way that feels wrong, stop that movement and use the alternate in the app. This is general coaching, not medical advice, so check with a doctor first if you have an injury or a health condition.

Warrior|7.notes: Purpose: full rest. This is when your body repairs and gets stronger, so treat it as part of the program. Sleep 7 to 9 hours, eat enough protein (a palm-sized portion at each meal), drink water through the day, and spend some time with family or outside. An easy walk or stretch is fine if you want it. Do not feel guilty. Rest days are how progress happens.
